BrickLane Retailers - Q3 FY2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, everyone, and welcome to the BrickLane Retailers Q3 FY2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] Please also note, today's event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Thompson, Investor Relations Director. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson, Investor Relations Director:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, and thank you for joining us today to discuss BrickLane Retailers' results for the Q3 FY2024. Joining me on today’s call are Jonathan Hale, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Rivera, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Merchandising Officer; and David Patel, Chief Stores Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call contains forward-looking statements, which are subject to risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

With that, I’ll turn the call over to Jonathan Hale.

Jonathan Hale, Chief Executive Officer:
Thank you, Sarah. Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I’m pleased to report BrickLane Retailers' performance for the Q3 FY2024. We continued to execute on our strategic priorities and delivered solid results despite the challenging macroeconomic environment.

Today I will cover six key aspects of our performance:

1. Comparable store sales growth year-over-year came in at a strong 4.2%, accelerating from prior quarters and reflecting broad-based strength across categories.

2. Sales per square foot reached $428, up 8.2% from last year, highlighting our productivity gains in the physical footprint.

3. On store footprint, we added a net three doors this quarter through 12 openings and nine closures, as part of disciplined optimization.

4. Our store remodel program advanced with 145 completions year-to-date, on pace for 180 by year-end, driving outsized comps in upgraded locations.

5. Gross margins expanded 140 basis points to 38.2%, thanks to better mix and efficiencies.

6. Across our key strategic initiatives, we made meaningful progress on omnichannel, portfolio optimization, supply chain, and innovation, positioning us for sustained growth.

We are confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Michael Rivera to provide more details on our financial results.

Michael Rivera, Chief Financial Officer:
Thank you, Jonathan. Good morning. I'll provide a more detailed review of our financial performance for the Q3 FY2024.

Our total revenue for the quarter was $2.75 billion, a 4.8% increase compared to the same period last year. Gross margin was 38.2%, representing a 140 basis point improvement year-over-year, primarily driven by stronger merchandise mix, reduced shrinkage, and supply chain efficiencies. Operating expenses were $1.82 billion, representing 66.2% of revenue. Net income was $195 million, or $1.35 per share. We generated $385 million in cash flow from operations. Inventory levels are currently well-controlled at about 12 weeks of supply, reflecting disciplined management.

To give you more color on these results and tie back to Jonathan's highlights, let me start with our comparable store sales growth on a year-over-year basis. For stores open at least 14 full months, we posted positive 4.2% comps growth this quarter, which builds on our fourth straight quarter of gains and picks up from 2.8% in Q2. Stacking two years, that's a healthy 12.4% increase, even as we compare against strong pandemic-era numbers.

Diving into segments, apparel and accessories grew 3.5%, powered by 2.1% traffic gains and 1.3% higher average unit retail. Women's activewear and denim led the way, with partner brands showing double-digit increases in dedicated zones, while men's held back slightly by unseasonal warmth but supported by smarter markdown controls that cut clearance by 150 basis points. Home and hardlines surged 6.8% on 4.2% traffic and 2.4% pricing power, echoing trends at home improvement leaders, especially in kitchen items and outdoor setups via our private-label growth. Beauty and wellness added 4.1% through higher average unit retail on prestige expansions like mini-shops with key partners, boosted by app-driven personalization. Footwear dipped 0.5% from category saturation, but new exclusives are ramping now.

Traffic overall rose 2.7%, beating industry benchmarks, thanks to our rewards program with 28 million members fueling 62% of comp sales. Transaction values climbed 1.4% to $68.42, aided by digital kiosks and BOPIS, which made up 18% of sales and added 90 basis points to store comps. Regionally, the Northeast shone at 5.6% with remodel tailwinds and tourism; Southeast at 4.9% post-weather recovery; Midwest at 2.1% holding firm in urban spots; West Coast at 3.2% resilient despite cost pressures.

Key enablers included our optimization efforts with tech upgrades improving conversions by over 3%, direct vendor shipping cutting stockouts 40%, and everyday low pricing gaining us share. We outperformed peers and guide Q4 comps to 3% to 4.5%, with holiday momentum.

Shifting to sales per square foot, a key productivity gauge calculated on net sales over average selling space, we hit $428 this quarter, up 8.2% year-over-year from $396 and 2.1% from Q2's $419. That's 11 straight quarters of growth, topping industry averages and landing us top-quartile among peers.

Roughly 60% of the gain traced to traffic up 5.3% and conversion at 28.1%, via app marketing and optimized layouts in lifestyle zones blending apparel with home. The rest came from owned brands at 42% of sales with margin premiums, plus RFID curbing shrink. Sunbelt stores led at $465, up 11.4%, on migration demand; Northeast at $402 with format tweaks; Midwest/PNW at $391 gaining share via experiences. We're closing low performers, redeploying to high-velocity small formats testing at $510 run rates, with tech like computer vision set to add more. Guide full-year $430 to $442.

On our store footprint, we opened 12 locations and closed nine in Q3 for a net add of three, versus 18 and 12 last year. Year-to-date, 42 openings and 28 closures net 14, bringing us to 1,287 U.S. doors averaging 28,500 square feet as we favor compact formats. Apparel/footwear took most openings, home hubs the rest; closures hit low-productivity discount spots under $450 per square foot.

Sunbelt focus with 70% of opens in growth areas like Phoenix and Atlanta yielding 8.2% comps; Northeast closures in weak malls. New doors show 25% better EBITDA margins via RFID, ship-from-store, and rent deals. Full-year net 18-22 adds; 2024 flat with optimization saving $75 million in leases.

Regarding store remodel and renovation plans, these are central to our multi-year push for comps, omnichannel, and defending against e-tailers. Our 1,200-plus big-box stores average 95,000 square feet in home goods and merchandise. Traffic's back to 92% of 2019, but conversions need experiential boosts. FY2024 capex is $450 million, up 15%, for remodels/relocations—4.2% of $10.7 billion revenue guide. Completed 145 full overhauls YTD, targeting 180 by year-end at $2.8 million each.

Upgrades include 30% space to high-margin shop-in-shops yielding 12% adjacent lifts; RFID smart shelves cutting out-of-stocks 22% and syncing BOPIS; AI signage boosting baskets 8%; mobile POS slashing times to 90 seconds and throughput 18%, lifting EBITDA margins 4.5 points. Results: 9.2% comps vs. 2.1% non-remodeled, sales per foot from $420 to $478, NPS to 78.

'BrickLane 2.0' eyes 450 stores over three years at $2.5-3.2 million each, prioritizing high-ROI via analytics, 15-20 relocations/year to 85,000 square feet; 40% recycled materials, 25% energy cuts for $15 million incentives and 14% higher eco spend. Northeast small pilots +11% comps with BOPIS/EV; Southeast/Midwest 120 in FY2025 with resilient/local merch; West premium demos +7% units; Sunbelt new-builds 12-15% IRR. 2-3x ROI in 24 months, $100 million labor savings, funded by $650 million FCF.

Now, more on gross margins at 38.2%, up 140 basis points from 36.8%—third straight expansion under our Margin Resilience Initiative against inflation.

Merchandise margins rose 110 basis points to 41.5% on mix shift: private labels at 28% sales, like Home Essentials at 52% margins vs. 38% branded; promotions down to 12% via AI pricing. Shrink fell 15 basis points to 1.4% with RFID in 85% stores cutting losses 25%. Freight eased 8%, nearshoring to 65% softlines, vendor rebates adding 50 basis points.

Sunbelt +180 bps to 39.8% on traffic; Northeast +90 bps to 37.1%; Canada steady at 37.5%. Store 2.0 remodels aid via high-margin space/BOPIS. Expect 100-150 bps more next quarter toward mid-40s long-term.

Wrapping with key strategic initiatives across four pillars, delivering 420 basis points EBITDA margin gain to 8.2%. Omnichannel at 28% sales, up from 22%; BOPIS 42% of e-comm, +15% conversions, same-day curbside 85% stores, +12% visits; $150 million more for 35% digital. Stores: 72% sales, $650/sq ft; 175 NextGen remodels +14-18% sales/250 bps margins; 22 small formats +9% traffic; net 50 stores FY2024, Sunbelt focus. Supply chain: vendor inflation 4.2%, 96% on-time, turns 5.8x, 63 days inventory; 65% North America sourcing, three micro-fulfillment centers -22% last-mile, private EcoForge +28%. Innovation: app 14 million users +25%, bundles +19% ticket to $128; headless CMS 2x ROI; recycled line $450 million +35%; loyalty 18 million, 62% redemption +150 bps comps.

Maintaining strong balance sheet, positioned for growth.

Now, I'd like to hand it over to Lisa Chen, our Chief Merchandising Officer, to discuss our new product lines, and after that to David Patel to discuss store operations.

Lisa Chen, Chief Merchandising Officer:
Thank you, Michael. This quarter, we launched our expanded EcoForge sustainable home essentials line, which has seen strong uptake with 28% growth and 55% gross margins, driving category share and appealing to younger shoppers. We're excited about the potential of this and other upcoming private-label launches in kitchen and apparel.

David Patel, Chief Stores Officer:
Thank you, Lisa. We continue to focus on improving the customer experience in our stores. We have implemented frictionless checkout lanes and experiential demo zones in remodeled units, and we're seeing positive results with dwell times up 16%, conversions improving, and early EBITDA lifts.

Now, let's open the line for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from Emily Carter with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter (Goldman Sachs):
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the impact of e-commerce growth on your sales?

Jonathan Hale, Chief Executive Officer:
Good morning, Emily. E-commerce remains a headwind at 22-28% of category sales, but our omnichannel acceleration has turned it into a tailwind. Digital is now 28% of our total, with BOPIS and curbside driving store traffic up 12% and capturing fulfillment efficiencies. Remodels blend digital touchpoints like AR and smart shelves, delivering 9%+ comps spreads. We're gaining share through integrated experiences that pure plays can't match.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mark Lee with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Mark Lee (JPMorgan):
What are your expectations for same-store sales growth in the next quarter?

Michael Rivera, Chief Financial Officer:
Thanks, Mark. We're guiding Q4 comps to 3% to 4.5%, with upside from holiday events and remodel ramp. This assumes modest traffic gains, anchored by loyalty and omnichannel, plus strength in home categories. Broader macro like sentiment stabilization supports mid-single digits into 2025.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Sarah Kim with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Sarah Kim (Morgan Stanley):
Can you elaborate on the supply chain improvements?

Jonathan Hale, Chief Executive Officer:
Absolutely, Sarah. We've boosted on-time delivery to 96% with AI forecasting, accelerated inventory turns to 5.8x and down to 63 days on hand. Nearshoring 65% sourcing cuts freight risks, micro-fulfillment centers trim last-mile 22%, and vendor scorecards ensure resilience. This supports 97% in-stocks on core items and margin gains.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Wong with Barclays. Please go ahead.

David Wong (Barclays):
What is the impact from the loyalty program?

Jonathan Hale, Chief Executive Officer:
Great question, David. Our program grew to 18 million members, driving 62% of comp sales and 150 basis points of uplift. App personalization boosts tickets 19% to $128, redemptions at 62%, with Gen Z focus via sustainability adding loyalty. It's core to our customer-centric pillar.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Alex Rivera with BofA Securities. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera (BofA Securities):
Thanks. On remodels, how are you thinking about ROI and pace into next year?

Michael Rivera, Chief Financial Officer:
Hi Alex. Remodeled stores are running 720 basis point comp spreads, sales per foot up to $478, and 2-3x ROI in 24 months from lifts plus $100 million labor savings. FY2025 accelerates to 120+ in heartland regions, funded organically, with geospatial targeting high-traffic sites for 10%+ fleet IRR.

Operator:
Thank you. That concludes today's questions.

Jonathan Hale, Chief Executive Officer:
Thank you for your questions. In closing, we are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain focused on executing our long-term strategy. Thank you for your continued support.

Sarah Thompson, Investor Relations Director:
This concludes today's call. Thank you for joining us.
